correctness.rationale: The matrix model for \(\operatorname{Aut}(C_{p^a}\oplus C_{p^b})\) is the published one for distinct exponents. The proof partitions all automorphisms into the four residue patterns for \(\alpha-1\) and \(\delta-1\). When one diagonal difference is a unit, elimination reduces the fixed subgroup to one scalar congruence and the valuation-one condition is counted exactly. When both are divisible by \(p\), either the image lies in \(pA\), or an explicit surjection from the cokernel onto \(C_{p^2}\) rules out a kernel of order \(p\), except when \(b-a=1\) and both off-diagonal parameters are units; that remaining case is solved directly and has exactly \(p\) fixed points. The disjoint case counts sum to the displayed formula, and exhaustive finite replays match every branch and the known small-exponent formulas.

originality.rationale: The 2018 source proves only the fixed-point-free multiplicity for arbitrary distinct rank-two exponents and explicitly asks for general exact \(\theta\)-formulas. The known all-\(\theta\) calculations cover \(C_p\oplus C_{p^2}\), \(C_p\oplus C_{p^3}\), and \(C_{p^2}\oplus C_{p^3}\), all recovered as special cases. The 2023 Reidemeister-spectrum theorem determines occurrence of fixed-point cardinalities, not multiplicities of automorphisms realizing them. Targeted searches did not locate the arbitrary-\((a,b)\) exactly-\(p\) multiplicity formula.

value.rationale: The invariant \(\theta(A,d)\) is explicitly motivated by a published exact-formula question. The result settles the first nontrivial fixed-point cardinality \(d=p\) for every rank-two finite abelian \(p\)-group with distinct exponents, strictly extending three isolated exact computations. The answer is not a routine parameter substitution: it changes with whether \(a=1\) and whether the exponent gap is one, and in characteristic two it yields the sharp structural criterion \(b=a+1\) for the existence of an automorphism with exactly two fixed points.
